description: Project-authored regression examples with expected and acceptable capability labels. These are not independently annotated job data or model-training examples. Screenshot cases are development regressions; the other cases exercise different wording and domains.

cases.text: Software Engineer / Developer. Full-Stack Sorcerer. You will write clean code, delete it, rewrite it, and wonder why it worked the first time in staging but burst into flames in production. Attend 15 meetings a week to discuss why a button should be 2 pixels to the left. Google error messages that nobody has asked about since 2014. Negotiate peace treaties between the frontend and backend teams.

Marketing / Brand Manager. Grandmaster of Buzzwords & Brand Evangelist. Convince people that our normal product is actually a life-altering paradigm shift. Post on LinkedIn about synergistic ecosystem alignment while drinking your third iced coffee. Measure metrics that go up and down for reasons science cannot explain. Turn a 3-word product update into a 12-slide keynote presentation.

Customer Support / Success. Professional Apologist & Chief Vibe Officer. Stand in the line of fire and smile while users explain why our software ruined their entire Tuesday. Tell people to try clearing their cache for the 400th time today. Translate angry ALL-CAPS emails into calm, polite corporate poetry. Turn weeping customers into brand loyalists using sheer empathy and patience.
Backend developer. Persuade the database to stop taking coffee breaks when traffic arrives. Track down intermittent query failures and keep the service responding.
You will babysit dashboards that insist everything is fine while the service is on fire. Investigate alerts and restore the application when it fails.
Create backend application features and refactor legacy source code. Investigate reported software defects and implement fixes.
Build automated regression tests, reproduce defects and verify expected behaviour before each release.
Revise screen layouts and button positions so that visitors can navigate the application easily.
Examine weekly sales metrics, compare performance trends and explain unusual changes in the figures.
Write promotional messages that explain our product benefits and persuade potential customers to try it.
Schedule posts for our social networks and answer comments from the online community.
Summarise project findings in slide decks and deliver clear presentations to our stakeholders.
Respond to customer complaints and patiently guide users through fixing problems with their purchases.
Rewrite confusing instructions into clear emails and adjust the tone for different recipients.
Acknowledge people's frustration, listen patiently and respond with understanding when they are upset.
Help colleagues resolve disagreements and bring competing departments together around a shared solution.
Your calendar will resemble a game of Tetris. Prioritise competing deadlines and keep tasks moving when requests arrive together.
Be the last line of defence against the missing decimal point. Check invoices carefully and correct inconsistent figures before approval.
New starters will think the internal tools were designed by aliens. Show them how the process works and explain each step patiently.
Discuss pricing and contract conditions with suppliers to reach terms acceptable to both sides.
Break projects into tasks, allocate budgets and people, and follow delivery dates through to completion.
Gather evidence from reliable sources, compare findings and document your conclusions about unfamiliar subjects.
Learn unfamiliar workflows quickly and adjust constructively when priorities and instructions change.
Keep trying when difficult tasks encounter setbacks and follow through until the work is complete.

Benefits:
We offer programming courses, customer support training and free presentation workshops.
Programming is not required for this role. We do not handle customer complaints. No presentations are needed.
Software Engineer / Developer. Marketing / Brand Manager. Customer Support / Success.
We need someone good at things who can do the work well.
The coffee machine is our unofficial manager. Biscuits have mysteriously disappeared again. Bring your favourite mug on Monday.
Applicants must cast spells and tame dragons while riding a unicorn through the clouds.
Yesterday I watched a film about a detective and ate popcorn with my friends.

About us:
We write software and resolve customer complaints across the world.

Enjoy classes on negotiation and marketing communication.
